draft.title: Attributions
card: An attribution is the reason we give for why someone behaved the way they did. It is a quick explanation, and it may or may not be correct.
the cause is put down to the person, such as their personality, mood, effort or ability.
the cause is put down to the situation, such as the weather, other people, luck or a task that is hard.

The fundamental attribution error is leaning too far toward internal causes when judging other people, and not giving enough weight to the situation. We tend to do this less when explaining our own behaviour.
draft.remember: An attribution names a cause. Judging others, we tend to over-pick the person and under-pick the situation.

a.q: Sam is late to class. Jo thinks, "Sam is lazy and never plans ahead." What type of attribution is this?
opts: Internal, because it blames Sam's personality
External, because it blames Sam's lateness
Internal, because it blames the time of day
External, because it blames Sam's lack of effort
a.why: Jo explains the lateness by a trait of Sam, being lazy, so the attribution is internal. It is not external, because Jo names no situation such as a delayed train.
a.clue: Does Jo point to Sam or to the circumstances?

b.q: Priya sees a driver cut in front of her and thinks, "What a selfish person." Later she cuts in front of someone herself and thinks, "I had to, the lane was ending." Which description fits best?
opts: She leans toward internal causes for the other driver
She leans toward external causes for the other driver
She uses internal causes for both drivers
She uses external causes for both drivers
b.why: She blames the other driver's character, which is internal, but blames the lane for her own action, which is external. Leaning toward the person when judging others is the fundamental attribution error. She does not use the same type of cause for both drivers.
b.clue: Compare the cause she gives for the other driver with the one she gives for herself.

a.best: Internal, because it blames Sam's personality

b.best: She leans toward internal causes for the other driver
